purpose: Guide a phase specification that distinguishes inherited behavior from deliberate deltas and covers compatibility, regression, measurement, and safe release.

ordered_sections.title: Phase identity and inherited baseline
ordered_sections.purpose: Record document control, authoritative source requirements, terminology, prior-phase scope, and approval status.

ordered_sections.title: Phase objective and rationale
ordered_sections.purpose: Explain the intended outcome and connect prior learning or an explicit no-learning exception to the phase decision.

ordered_sections.title: Inherited-behavior register
ordered_sections.purpose: Identify behavior that remains authoritative and unchanged for this phase.

ordered_sections.title: Delta register
ordered_sections.purpose: Classify each affected behavior as modified, added, deprecated, or removed and state its rationale.

ordered_sections.title: Changed flows
ordered_sections.purpose: Show how the phase changes observable customer, system, or operational flows.

ordered_sections.title: Added and modified requirements
ordered_sections.purpose: Specify atomic, traceable, prioritized, and verifiable changes with acceptance and test scenarios.

ordered_sections.title: Compatibility, migration, and regression behavior
ordered_sections.purpose: Define coexistence, transition, preserved behavior, failure handling, accessibility, and regression coverage.

ordered_sections.title: Delta metrics and telemetry
ordered_sections.purpose: Measure changed outcomes and verify that inherited behavior remains within guardrails.

ordered_sections.title: Rollout, rollback, operational ownership, and open decisions
ordered_sections.purpose: Define release control, recovery, verification, sign-off, owners, and unresolved choices.

narrative_rules: Organize the document around inherited behavior and explicit deltas rather than restating the full prior specification.
Connect prior learning to the phase decision and then to each delta, or record an approved no-prior-learning exception.
Assign every affected behavior exactly one lifecycle state: inherited unchanged, modified, added, deprecated, or removed.
Derive added or modified requirements from authoritative source needs and numbered use cases.
Keep each changed requirement singular, observable, necessary or explicitly optional, prioritized, and verifiable.
Explain compatibility and regression consequences for both changed and inherited behavior.
Separate stakeholder-driven deltas from system-design implementation choices.
Include negative, boundary, accessibility, error, migration, and recovery behavior where applicable.
evidence_rules: Trace each delta to a source need, learning, decision, use case, requirement, test, and measure as applicable.
Keep prior results, current observations, assumptions, targets, and commitments in separate evidence states.
For delta measures, retain definition, population, period, grain, comparator, source, freshness, and caveat.
Use explicit evidence to show whether inherited behavior remains within its guardrails.
Do not invent prior-phase learning when none is available; use the documented exception path.
terminology_rules: Use stable identifiers for inherited behaviors, deltas, source needs, use cases, requirements, tests, metrics, and dependencies.
Use only the defined lifecycle states for affected behavior.
Distinguish inherited baseline, compatibility behavior, migration behavior, regression coverage, and new scope.
Expand acronyms at first use unless an approved glossary marks them as established.
formatting_rules: Use separate registers for inherited behavior and deltas.
Show old and new behavior together when a comparison is required to understand a change.
Number requirements, acceptance criteria, tests, metrics, and dependencies for traceability.
Use tables for lifecycle state, traceability, compatibility, migration, and regression coverage.
Keep rationale and causal reasoning in prose.
Apply the current organization template before default product-document formatting.
hard_fail_rules: Block publication when changed behavior lacks an inheritance or delta lifecycle state.
Block publication when neither a learning-to-decision-to-delta chain nor an approved no-prior-learning exception exists.
Block publication when an added or modified requirement is compound, ambiguous, unobservable, or unverifiable.
Block publication when traceability from source need through verification is missing for a changed behavior.
Block publication when rollout lacks rollback, compatibility, or regression coverage.
Block publication when evidence is fabricated, untraceable, mislabeled, or missing critical context.
Block publication when body text and tables conflict or a material contradiction remains unresolved.
Block publication when a date, owner, target, fact, or commitment is silently introduced.
Block publication when required overview context is absent without an approved exception.
Block publication when source-specific sample facts appear in a new artifact.
Block publication when language repair changes a requirement, decision, or protected fact.
Block any full-language-conformance status unless the configured bundle, checks, exceptions, and human review are approved.
